note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. `hasCriticalFinding` requires severe OSA (AHI >= 30) TOGETHER WITH significant desaturation (or nocturnal hypoventilation alone) — severe OSA on its own (no significant desaturation) still grades major severity via the AHI severity band (R-SEV-MAJOR-02) but never trips the critical predicate, so it escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, not 'critical-alert'. The second persona below isolates exactly that distinction.

personas.name: normal-home-sleep-apnoea-test-complete
personas.description: A home sleep apnoea test for reported snoring with no witnessed apnoeas or daytime sleepiness: AHI 3.2 (normal range), no significant desaturation, every mandatory report section present — expect normal classification + none severity + 100% completeness + routine follow-up + no-action.

state.impression: Normal home sleep apnoea test; no evidence of obstructive sleep apnoea.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No further sleep-study follow-up required for this indication.

personas.name: abnormal-severe-osa-no-desaturation-major-not-critical-complete
personas.description: Attended polysomnography for loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas, and excessive daytime sleepiness confirms severe obstructive sleep apnoea (AHI 42) without significant desaturation (minimum SpO2 88%): `hasCriticalFinding` requires severe OSA together with significant desaturation specifically, so this grades major severity via the AHI severity band alone but never trips the critical predicate — it escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, not 'critical-alert'; report complete — expect abnormal classification + major severity (reportingCategory Severe OSA (AHI >=30)) + 100% completeness + urgent follow-up + specialist-referral.

state.clinicalHistory: Loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas, and excessive daytime sleepiness (Epworth 16/24); attended polysomnography to confirm suspected severe OSA.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: No previous sleep study on file.
state.findingsNarrative: Frequent obstructive apnoeas and hypopnoeas throughout the recording, AHI 42 (severe), predominantly supine and REM-related. Oxygen desaturation index 38; minimum SpO2 88%, without sustained or significant desaturation.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Refer to the sleep clinic for CPAP titration; advise on DVLA driving implications pending treatment.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent sleep-clinic review for CPAP titration and advise on DVLA driving implications.

personas.name: critical-severe-osa-significant-desaturation-uncommunicated-incomplete
personas.description: Polysomnography shows very frequent obstructive apnoeas and hypopnoeas (AHI 65, severe) with profound and sustained oxygen desaturation — minimum SpO2 71%, 95 minutes spent below 90% SpO2: severe OSA together with significant desaturation is a critical finding that auto-escalates classification to critical and follow-up to critical-alert regardless of the other axes, with the recommended action naming an urgent CPAP / ventilation review and DVLA driving implications; the result has not yet been recorded as communicated, no originating request is linked, and the clinical history, comparison, and impression sections are not yet completed while urgent CPAP initiation is arranged — expect critical classification + major severity + 40% completeness + critical-alert follow-up + urgent-review.

state.findingsNarrative: Very frequent obstructive apnoeas and hypopnoeas throughout the recording, AHI 65 (severe), with profound and sustained oxygen desaturation: minimum SpO2 71%, 95 minutes spent below 90% SpO2.
state.clinicianNotes: Phoned through to the on-call respiratory team immediately; urgent CPAP initiation being arranged and patient advised not to drive pending treatment.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange an urgent CPAP / ventilation review, communicate the critical result directly to the referrer now and document the conversation, and advise on occupational-driver (DVLA) implications.
